strengths: Originality: Choosing column spacings inversely proportional to Cholesky diagonals provides an elegant connection between GPTQ/SIC and Gaussian rate–distortion theory. The arithmetic–geometric mean characterization gives useful insight into when equal-spacing quantization is inefficient, beyond simply proposing another quantizer.

Significance: The reported compression–quality improvements are substantial across four models. For example, Llama-3.2-1B reaches perplexity 16.19 at 2.00 bits versus QTIP's 18.67 at 2.02 bits; Qwen3-8B reaches 11.37 versus Huffman-GPTQ's 13.97 at 2.125 bits. Tables 9–10 also demonstrate downstream benefits, particularly at low rates.

Presentation and reproducibility: The manuscript explains the practical corrections, provides algorithm pseudocode, and documents calibration data, damping, rate searches, and mixing optimization. Table 6 usefully checks whether standard codecs approach the reported entropy estimates.

Limitations and ethics: The paper explicitly acknowledges the Gaussian weight assumption, limited model scale, and absence of hardware throughput measurements. These are appropriate disclosures, and no material research-ethics concern is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness of the central guarantee: The abstract claims a 0.255-bit gap uniformly over all activation covariance matrices, whereas Theorem 3.3 concerns a high-rate limit for Gaussian weights and asymptotically many rows. A covariance-independent limiting constant does not establish uniform convergence over covariance matrices or a finite-rate guarantee at the evaluated 1–4 bits. Moreover, the theorem states positive semidefinite covariance, although its construction divides by Cholesky diagonals and its proof uses inverses and a positive determinant. Singular covariances require separate treatment. The headline claim should be narrowed to the result actually established.

Mathematical presentation needs substantive correction. Equations (41), (42), and (57) subtract log(alpha) from entropy, although entropy grows as -log(alpha), so the finite limit requires adding log(alpha). Section 3.1 defines the transformed reconstruction using an inverse rather than the matching forward transform, and the Section 4 rescaler objective omits the quadratic reconstruction term that appears in Algorithm 4. These appear repairable, but they impede verification of a paper whose primary contribution is theoretical. The rate definition also needs consistent per-weight normalization and explicit coding assumptions.

The experiments do not isolate the proposed unequal-rate allocation. Full WaterSIC includes shrinkage, drift correction, residual compensation, optimized rescalers, attention weighting, adaptive mixing, and feature erasure. Figures 7–11 primarily ablate selected additions using activation MSE at approximately 4 bits; they do not compare equal versus unequal spacings within an otherwise identical pipeline at matched rates. Consequently, the evidence does not establish how much of the low-rate perplexity improvement comes from the central innovation. The claim that gains are additive with better quantizers or fine-tuning is also untested.

The broad state-of-the-art claim exceeds the comparison coverage. Qwen3-8B is compared primarily with GPTQ/RTN variants, while stronger modern methods appear only for some other models. At 3.125 bits, WaterSIC loses to Huffman-GPTQ on four of seven downstream metrics in Table 10. The results support strong perplexity improvements over the evaluated baselines, but not uniformly superior downstream performance or comprehensive superiority across 1–4 bits.

Compression accounting remains incomplete. Main comparisons use estimated entropy for WaterSIC and stored code cardinality for several competitors. Table 6 partially validates this choice, but only for two layers of one model at one target rate; actual codec sizes exceed entropy estimates. Complete serialized model sizes, including metadata and any unquantized parameters, are needed to establish matched-storage comparisons, particularly where high-rate improvements are small.

Practical reproducibility and cost are insufficiently established. The method uses the full WikiText-2 training split and repeated requantization and attention forward passes during per-layer searches, but reports no quantization runtime or peak memory. The manuscript provides no implementation link, and downstream evaluation settings are less detailed than the calibration procedure. These omissions make it difficult to reproduce the reported frontier and assess its computational tradeoff.

Presentation and reproducibility: The manuscript explains the core algorithm intuitively and supplies pseudocode, calibration procedures, search settings, diagnostic plots, and practical compression measurements. These are valuable implementation details.

Soundness—mathematical inconsistencies: Equations (41), (42), (55), and (57) subtract log(alpha) from the quantized entropy, whereas the finite high-resolution limit requires adding log(alpha). These expressions already fail for a one-dimensional Gaussian as alpha approaches zero. Section 3.1 also defines the transformed reconstruction using an inverse that does not yield the stated distortion identity, and Section 4’s displayed rescaler objective omits the quadratic reconstruction term used in the subsequent updates. These appear repairable, but the derivation needs a careful correction before it can serve as a reliable theoretical reference.

Experimental attribution: The introduction says the setting isolates unequal quantization rates, but the reported method additionally uses optimized rescalers, activation-drift and residual corrections, attention weighting, adaptive mixing, and feature erasure. Figures 7–11 examine activation MSE, predominantly at approximately 4 bits; they do not provide a matched-rate perplexity or downstream ablation of equal versus unequal spacing under otherwise identical processing. Consequently, the central innovation’s contribution to the low-bit gains remains unclear.

Comparison strength: Qwen3-8B baselines are imported from prior work, while WaterSIC uses extensive calibration and model-specific outlier removal. The manuscript does not demonstrate matched calibration resources or equivalent preprocessing. Its broad state-of-the-art claim also exceeds the tested baseline set, and downstream superiority is mixed at higher rates: in Table 10 at 3.125 bits, WaterSIC trails Huffman-GPTQ on four of seven tasks.

Storage accounting and practical significance: Main comparisons use empirical entropy for WaterSIC against fixed-width storage rates for several alternatives. This is a legitimate compression direction, but realized storage must substantiate close frontier comparisons. Table 6 checks only two layers of one model at approximately 2 bits and shows codec overhead above entropy. Complete serialized model sizes, including metadata and unquantized parameters, are not sufficiently documented. The acknowledged absence of throughput measurements further limits conclusions about deployment benefits.

Reproducibility and presentation: No implementation link, quantization runtime, peak-memory measurements, or repeated-run variability is supplied. Section 5 describes WikiText-2 validation perplexity, whereas Appendix D specifies the test split. Algorithm 3 mixes i and k indices, and its damping prescription is not consistent with Appendix C’s instruction to modify all relevant covariance matrices. Together with the theoretical errors, these ambiguities require revision despite the otherwise extensive appendix.

strengths: Originality: Choosing per-column spacings inversely proportional to Cholesky diagonals provides an elegant connection between successive interference cancellation and rate allocation. The arithmetic-versus-geometric mean analysis offers useful understanding of when equal-spacing entropy-coded GPTQ can be inefficient.

Significance: Reported perplexity improvements span four models and are substantial at low rates. Examples include 16.19 versus QTIP's 18.67 at approximately 2 bits on Llama-3.2-1B (Table 1), and 11.37 versus Huffman-GPTQ's 13.97 at 2.125 bits on Qwen3-8B (Table 2). Downstream evaluations provide additional evidence, particularly at low rates (Tables 9–10).

Presentation and reproducibility: The manuscript explains the practical corrections in detail and supplies algorithm descriptions, calibration procedures, search settings, and diagnostic ablations. Table 6 usefully checks entropy estimates against actual lossless compression.

Limitations and ethics: The paper explicitly acknowledges missing inference-throughput measurements, larger-model evaluations, and comparisons with some fine-tuning methods. These are appropriate disclosures. I see no material research-ethics concern specific to the contribution.
weaknesses: Soundness—the headline guarantee exceeds the established result. Theorem 3.3 concerns a high-rate limit for iid Gaussian weights, with an additional large-row-count limit. It does not establish a 0.255-bit bound at the practical 1–4-bit operating points or for trained LLM weights. Moreover, a covariance-independent limiting constant for each fixed covariance does not establish uniform convergence over covariances. The abstract's unrestricted near-optimality language and the suggested implications for model-quality Pareto frontiers need substantial qualification.

Soundness—the theoretical statements require correction. Theorem 3.3 is stated for every positive semidefinite covariance, but the algorithm and proof divide by Cholesky diagonals and use inverses and determinants; singular covariances are not covered as written. The zero covariance is an immediate counterexample to the claimed universal gap equality. Appendix B also repeatedly uses H(Z) minus log(alpha), whereas high-resolution quantization requires H(Z) plus log(alpha) to approach a finite constant (Equations 41–42 and 55–57). Section 3.1's transformed reconstruction uses an inverse where multiplication by V Lambda^(1/2) is needed. These appear repairable, but the central theorem and proof are not correct as presented.

Experimental attribution: The evaluated method combines unequal rates with rescaler optimization, activation-drift and residual corrections, attention weighting, adaptive mixing, and feature erasure. Figures 7–11 mainly measure activation MSE, largely at approximately 4 bits; they do not isolate the proposed rate allocation through matched-rate perplexity and downstream comparisons against an otherwise identical equal-spacing pipeline. Consequently, the assertion that the experiments isolate the central innovation, and that its gains are additive with other improvements, is unsupported.

Comparison fairness and significance: WaterSIC calibrates on the entire WikiText-2 training split and repeatedly searches per-layer parameters, while some baseline results are imported from other papers without demonstrating matched calibration data and computational budgets. Qwen3 additionally receives manually identified outlier-row removal, without a corresponding baseline control. Its main comparison also omits several stronger contemporary quantizers. The results support superiority over the evaluated configurations, rather than an unrestricted state-of-the-art claim.

Compression accounting: Most comparisons use estimated entropy for WaterSIC and fixed-code rates for other methods. This distinction is disclosed, but Table 6 checks only two layers of one model at one target rate and shows nonzero codec overhead. Complete serialized model sizes, including metadata and any unquantized parameters, are needed to establish the claimed storage frontier. The absence of throughput measurements appropriately limits deployment conclusions rather than invalidating the compression idea.

Reproducibility and presentation: No implementation link is provided in the manuscript, quantization runtime and peak memory are not reported, and evaluation software settings and variability are insufficiently documented. Section 5 calls the perplexity split validation, whereas Appendix D specifies test. Algorithm 3 also has inconsistent loop indices and does not transparently implement the cross-covariance damping prescribed in Appendix C. Together with the theoretical errors, these discrepancies make an independent implementation harder to verify.

strengths: Originality: The connection between unequal column precision, Cholesky innovation variances, and reverse waterfilling provides useful understanding of GPTQ. The AM–GM characterization explains when equal-spacing quantization wastes rate and motivates a simple allocation rule.

Soundness within a restricted setting: For fixed positive-definite activation covariance, iid Gaussian weights, and high-rate quantization, the analysis gives a plausible and informative explanation of the asymptotic scalar-quantization penalty. Detailed derivations and algorithms are provided.

Significance: The practical pipeline delivers substantial reported improvements across several model families and sizes. For example, Table 1 reports Llama-3.2-1B perplexity of 16.19 at 2 bits without finetuning, versus 18.67 for QTIP at 2.02 bits. Evaluation extends beyond WikiText-2 to C4 and downstream accuracy.

Reproducibility and limitations: The appendices describe calibration, hyperparameters, adaptive mixing, and finetuning in considerable detail. Calibration-domain sensitivity and missing hardware-throughput evaluation are acknowledged and investigated. No material research-ethics concern is evident.
weaknesses: The central guarantee is overstated. The abstract claims a gap of at most 0.255 bits uniformly over all activation covariances, whereas Theorem 3.3 establishes a pointwise high-rate limit for the Gaussian model, with an additional infinite-row limit. This does not establish a finite-rate guarantee at the evaluated 1–4-bit operating points, uniform convergence over covariance matrices, or a guarantee for the modified practical pipeline. Moreover, the theorem states positive semidefinite covariance, but its inverse-Cholesky and determinant expressions require nonsingularity; zero covariance directly contradicts the stated universal constant-gap equality.

The theoretical presentation needs correction before the proof can be reliably checked. Equations (41), (42), and (57) subtract log(alpha) from entropy, although entropy grows as minus log(alpha); the displayed finite limits require the opposite sign. Section 3.1 also defines the transformed reconstruction using an inverse where multiplication is needed for the claimed distortion identity. These appear repairable, but affect central derivations. The Gaussian histogram diagnostics in Appendix E establish neither independence nor isotropy of weight rows.

The experiments do not isolate the principal claimed innovation. Full WaterSIC combines unequal spacing with shrinkage, drift and residual corrections, rescaler optimization, attention weighting, adaptive mixing, and dead-feature removal. Appendix E mainly ablates these additions using activation MSE at approximately 4 bits. A matched comparison that changes only equal versus unequal spacing, reporting perplexity and downstream accuracy across rates, is needed to substantiate the introduction's attribution of gains to rate allocation.

The broad state-of-the-art claim is contradicted by the manuscript's own comparisons. In Table 10, PV-Tuning achieves WikiText-2/C4 perplexities of 6.99/8.29, while all listed WaterSIC variants are worse on both metrics. Table 13 also shows a substantial C4 deficit relative to PV-Tuning and QuIP#. These results support competitive performance in particular settings, rather than superiority throughout 1–4 bits.

Storage comparisons require stronger validation. Most results use empirical entropy rather than complete serialized model size. Table 6 usefully checks actual codecs, but only for two blocks of one model at 2 bits, and achieved rates exceed entropy estimates. Complete-model byte counts, including retained high-precision parameters and metadata, are needed to establish the claimed storage frontier. The acknowledged absence of throughput measurements appropriately limits deployment conclusions.

Several reproducibility and presentation inconsistencies remain. Table 1 reports 1-bit WaterSIC-FT perplexity of 30.47, whereas Tables 7 and 16 report 32.85 under apparently matching conditions. Algorithm 3 mixes i and k indices in its core update and does not match Appendix C's damping prescription. The abstract's 'code is available here' supplies no usable link in the provided PDF. Quantization runtime is also missing despite repeated requantization and attention-block evaluation during adaptive search.

strengths: Originality: The connection between activation-aware quantization, successive interference cancellation, and waterfilling provides useful understanding. Choosing column spacings inversely proportional to Cholesky diagonals gives a principled explanation of why equal-spacing entropy-coded GPTQ can waste bits.

Significance: The reported improvements are substantial in several settings. On Llama-3.2-1B, Table 1 reports perplexity 16.19 at 2 bits without finetuning, versus 18.67 for QTIP at 2.02 bits. On Qwen3-8B, Table 18 reports MMLU accuracy of 61.14 versus 52.99 for Huffman-GPTQ at 2.125 bits.

Evaluation breadth: The appendices extend the experiments to multiple model families, a 70B model, C4, and downstream accuracy benchmarks. The calibration-corpus experiments in Table 15 usefully document distribution sensitivity rather than concealing it.

Presentation and reproducibility: The conceptual algorithm is understandable, and the appendices provide proofs, pseudocode, calibration procedures, and many hyperparameters. The discussion appropriately acknowledges missing deployment-throughput measurements. I found no material research-ethics concern.
weaknesses: Soundness—central guarantee is overstated: The abstract claims a rate gap of at most 0.255 bits uniformly over all activation covariances. Theorem 3.3 instead gives a high-rate, infinite-row asymptotic result for Gaussian weights. Its proof fixes the covariance before taking the limit and supplies no uniform convergence bound or guarantee at the experimentally important 1–4-bit rates. Moreover, the theorem includes positive semidefinite matrices although the construction requires nonzero Cholesky diagonals and uses inverses and determinants. Singular covariances require separate treatment. The practical algorithm's additional modifications are also outside this guarantee.

Soundness—mathematical statements need correction: Section 3.1 defines the transformed reconstruction using the inverse of VΛ^(1/2), which does not yield the asserted distortion identity; both weights and reconstruction should receive the same transformation. Equations (41), (42), (55), and (57) subtract log α where the high-resolution entropy relation requires adding it. Section 4's displayed rescaler loss omits the quadratic reconstruction term that appears in Algorithm 4. These appear repairable, but the mathematical development is not correct as written.

Experimental attribution: The introduction says the experiments isolate unequal column rates, but the evaluated method also changes shrinkage, activation drift correction, residual compensation, diagonal rescaling, attention weighting, adaptive mixing, and dead-feature handling. Appendix E mainly ablates auxiliary components using activation MSE near 4 bits. It does not provide the decisive matched-budget comparison between equal and unequal spacing with all other components fixed, including perplexity and downstream accuracy at low rates. Thus the source of the headline gains remains insufficiently established.

Significance—SOTA claims exceed the evidence: The manuscript's own broader comparisons contradict an unqualified state-of-the-art claim. In Table 10, PV-Tuning achieves W2/C4 perplexities of 6.99/8.29 on Llama-3-8B, outperforming every listed WaterSIC variant at approximately 2 bits. Table 13 similarly shows a substantial C4 advantage for PV-Tuning and QuIP#. These results do not negate WaterSIC's usefulness, but the claims should distinguish improvements over selected scalar baselines from superiority over the strongest available methods.

Practical compression evidence remains incomplete: Main comparisons use estimated entropy for WaterSIC and nominal storage rates for several baselines. Table 6 partially validates entropy estimates, but actual codec rates exceed entropy—for example, 1.992 bits becomes 2.138 with Zstd—and covers only selected matrices at one target rate. Complete serialized model sizes, including unquantized parameters and metadata, are needed to substantiate closely spaced frontier comparisons. Quantization time and peak memory are also important given full-training-split calibration and repeated per-layer searches; these costs are not adequately quantified.

Reproducibility and presentation inconsistencies: Section 5 specifies WikiText-2 validation evaluation, whereas Appendix D specifies test evaluation. The 1-bit Llama-3.2-1B finetuned perplexity is 30.47 in Table 1 but 32.85 in Tables 7 and 16, without an explained protocol difference. Finetuning is described using both KL distillation and cross-entropy. These discrepancies should be reconciled, and uncertainty across calibration samples or seeds should be reported where small gains support superiority claims.

strengths: Originality: The connection between entropy-coded GPTQ, successive interference cancellation, and reverse waterfilling provides useful new understanding. Choosing column spacings inversely proportional to Cholesky diagonals removes the arithmetic–geometric mean penalty in the high-rate analysis without transmitting a dense rotation.

Significance: The reported improvements over Huffman-GPTQ are substantial. On Llama-3.2-1B, WaterSIC achieves WikiText-2 perplexity 11.83 at 2.50 bits versus 17.74 at 2.54 bits for Huffman-GPTQ (Table 1). On Qwen3-8B at 2.125 bits, MMLU improves from 52.99 to 61.14 without finetuning (Table 18). These support a useful practical contribution.

Evaluation: Experiments cover multiple Llama models, including 70B, and Qwen3-8B, with perplexity, downstream accuracy, calibration-corpus sensitivity, and component diagnostics. Tables 10–16 usefully expose cross-domain weaknesses rather than hiding them.

Presentation and reproducibility: The conceptual algorithm is simple, and the appendices provide extensive pseudocode, hyperparameters, calibration procedures, and finetuning settings. The discussion explicitly acknowledges missing hardware-throughput evaluation. No material research-ethics concern is apparent for this compression study.
weaknesses: Soundness of the central guarantee: The abstract claims a gap within 0.255 bits uniformly over all activation covariances, but Theorem 3.3 establishes a high-rate, large-row-count limit for Gaussian weights. Appendix B fixes the covariance-dependent lattice shape before taking the limit; it does not establish uniform convergence over covariances or a finite-rate guarantee at the experimentally relevant 1–4 bits. Moreover, the theorem includes positive semidefinite matrices, although the algorithm and proof require nonzero Cholesky diagonals and matrix inverses. Singular covariances need separate treatment. The claims should explicitly distinguish this asymptotic result for PlainWaterSIC from guarantees for the practical algorithm.

Technical presentation needs correction before the theory can be reliably reused. Equations (41), (42), (55), and (57) subtract log(alpha), whereas high-resolution quantization requires H(Z) + log(alpha) to approach differential entropy. Section 3.1 defines the transformed reconstruction using an inverse, although the distortion identity requires multiplication by V Lambda^(1/2). The main-text rescaler objective also omits its quadratic reconstruction term, which appears correctly in Algorithm 4. Several errors appear repairable, but they affect central derivations rather than peripheral exposition.

The experiments do not isolate the main proposed innovation. Appendix E ablates several practical corrections through activation-MSE plots, but does not provide a controlled comparison of equal versus Cholesky-adaptive spacing with identical entropy coding, damping, calibration, drift correction, and rescaler optimization. Consequently, the end-to-end improvements cannot confidently be attributed to unequal rate allocation. A matched ablation reporting perplexity and downstream accuracy is needed.

The universal state-of-the-art claim is contradicted by the manuscript's own comparisons. In Table 10, PV-Tuning achieves W2/C4 perplexities of 6.99/8.29, outperforming all listed WaterSIC variants on Llama-3-8B. Table 13 likewise shows stronger C4 results for several competitors. These do not erase WaterSIC's merits, but require a narrower claim. Comparisons drawn from other publications also need clearer matching of calibration data and optimization budgets.

Reproducibility and practical rate accounting remain incomplete. The abstract's 'code is available here' has no usable link in the supplied PDF. Section 5 specifies WikiText-2 validation whereas Appendix D specifies test, and low-rate finetuned results differ between Tables 1 and 7 without explanation. Main comparisons use entropy estimates; Table 6 verifies actual codec sizes only for two layers at one rate and shows nonzero overhead. Complete serialized model sizes, treatment of unquantized parameters, and quantization time/peak memory would make the claimed compression frontier more credible. The acknowledged absence of inference benchmarks limits deployment conclusions, rather than invalidating the compression objective itself.
